title: Adaptive request slicing and deferred affinity to reduce CPU path congestion
author: Priya Nair
description: Motivation: production traffic showed persistent CPU-side tail latency spikes under mixed short/long sequence workloads. Investigation pointed to three correlated bottlenecks: coarse-grained request serialization that forces full-copy paths, eager thread affinity/pinning of worker threads leading to imbalance during garbage bursts, and KV cache prewarm thrash when large in-flight prefixes queue up. This PR introduces three coordinated runtime changes to address these: 1) adaptive request slicing: split long inferences into small CPU-affine micro-slices that can be interleaved by the scheduler to reduce lock hold times and make batching more opportunistic; slices are a runtime-visible unit, not a user-facing change. 2) deferred affinity: worker threads avoid hard pinning during non-critical phases and only escalate to CPU-affinity when the slice enters the kernel-critical path (kernel exec + KV lookup) — this minimizes expensive handoffs and syscall churn. 3) on-demand serialization + lightweight copy-on-write frames: we replace the old eager full-object serialization with a lazy/path-dependent serializer that performs zero-copy for read-only buffers and only materializes copies on mutation. Complementing these are: small KV prefetch windows to warm hot prefixes for the upcoming slice set and scheduler heuristics that bias interleaving to keep the GPU/tokenizer hot while limiting CPU lock contention. This change is implemented in the runtime scheduler, serializer, and KV components and is backward compatible with existing request semantics. Implementation notes: adaptive slicing sits inside src/runtime/scheduler/slicer.rs and introduces a Slice struct with lifecycle hooks. The serializer change is in src/runtime/serializer/on_demand.rs and a new CopyOnWriteFrame wrapper. Deferred affinity logic is gated behind a runtime flag runtime.scheduler.deferred_affinity=false by default for conservative rollout and can be enabled per-node via node config. Safety: added unit and integration tests cover slice reassembly, serializer edge cases, and race windows around deferred affinity. Benchmarks: microbench harness under mixed short(<=64)/long(>1024) workloads shows p95 latency reduction from 82ms to 67ms (-18%), aggregate throughput improvement +14% at tail-preserving load, CPU syscalls and context-switches dropped ~23%, and steady-state median latency change <2%. On internal end-to-end L7 workload the change reduced observed CPU queuing delay by 26% and brought down incident-prone bursts in 95th tail by 30%. Rollout plan: feature-gated on node level; staged canary to 5% of traffic for 48h with an automated rollback threshold of +10% token-cost or +15% p95 latency. Related work: follows background from ENG-2467 and complements work in ENG-2503 on KV cache eviction policies. Backwards compatibility: no breaking changes to API. Migration: none required.

release_notes: Introduce adaptive request slicing to interleave long requests and reduce CPU-side lock contention; add deferred affinity to avoid unnecessary thread pinning during non-critical sections; implement on-demand serializer with copy-on-write frames to cut unnecessary copies; small KV prefetch windows to reduce prefix miss latency. Feature-gated and opt-in per-node.
bench_summary: p95 latency -18% (82ms -> 67ms) on mixed workloads; throughput +14% at p95-preserving load; CPU syscalls/context-switches -23%; KV miss tail reduced ~20% with prefetch windows.
notes: Runtime flag: runtime.scheduler.deferred_affinity (default=false). Enable on canary nodes via cluster config. Observability: new metrics runtime.slicer.slice_duration_ms and runtime.serializer.copy_events_total.
